To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the accuracy of the compensation of spherical aberration is the main factor for the attainable resolution of the probe-forming system of a STEM, that the compensation of chromatic aberration is the most critical aberration to be corrected, and that the accuracy of compensation of astigmatism is of secondary importance for the attainable spatial resolution of the probe.
for a probe forming system with a resolution of 0.1 nm, the residual aberrations should be smaller than 1 nm.

the residual aberrations in the aberration-corrector system can be compensated by the corrector itself and that the residual aberration coefficients of the probe-forming system can be corrected to the level required for the desired resolution by a dedicated corrector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following points: (1) The influence of residual aberrations on the probe size and probe-forming angle in an aberration-corrector equipped STEM.

the following topics: 1) the evaluation of the residual aberrations for the probe-forming system of a high-resolution STEM, 2) the investigation of the required accuracy of the compensation of the non-rotationally-symmetric aberrations, 3) the development of a method to determine the residual aberration coefficients of a probe-formation system and 4) the development of methods to compensate the residual aberrations.
the development of a corrector for the probe-forming system of a dedicated high-resolution aberration corrected STEM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a probe-forming aberration-corrector for STEM should be capable of reducing the spherical aberration Cs to about 10 mm and the chromatic aberration Cs to less than 0.5 mm.
the residual spherical aberration of the probe-forming lens has to be reduced to a level less than 1 mm.
the compensation of the residual aberrations is not only possible in principle, but also that the required accuracy can be achieved with today's technology and the required effort is not prohibitive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a probe-forming aberration-corrector, the accuracy of the compensation for the third-order spherical aberration and for the fifth-order axial coma has to be less than 10% of their respective values.
, in the future, the residual aberrations will have to be reduced to 0.01 nm for the spherical aberration, 1.0 nm for the chromatic aberration and 1.0 mrad for the astigmatism, respectively.
, if the aberration coefficients are known with an accuracy of about 0.1% and the beam deflections are measured with a similar accuracy, a resolution in the order of 0.1-0.2 nm can be expected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the residual aberrations in the probe-forming system have to be controlled to the level of a few pm in order to achieve the desired resolution.
the residual astigmatism has to be reduced to less than 1/100 of the residual spherical aberration in order to achieve the sub-Angström resolution.
the accuracy required to compensate for the residual aberration is very stringent.
